articles.title: Excellence Award for Nancy Lieu
articles.summary: Nancy Lieu received the SJAA Excellence Award for Outstanding Service on May 6, 2023, recognizing her invaluable contributions to the San Jose Astronomical Association. Since joining in 2018, she has been a dedicated solar astronomy volunteer, instrumental in training operators, and stepped up to cover the critical Volunteer Coordinator role. Her consistent efforts have significantly supported SJAA events and operations.

articles.title: SJAA Logo Wear
articles.summary: This article encourages members to create and wear custom SJAA logo wear to foster club pride, identify members, and serve as a conversation starter. It provides a step-by-step guide on how to download the official SJAA logo from the club's website, select an online logo-wear company, and customize various apparel and items with the logo, including options to add personal names. The goal is to increase the visibility of SJAA members at events and in public.

articles.title: Observation Report: The Box
articles.summary: Joe Fragola recounts his successful observation of "The Box" (Hickson 61), a tight group of four spiral galaxies forming a nearly perfect rectangle in the constellation Coma Berenices. He finally viewed this galaxy cluster after a Starry Nights star party on August 15, providing details on its components and their magnitudes. The galaxies, NGC 4173, NGC 4169, NGC 4175, and NGC 4174, are all contained within a small field of view.

articles.title: Stars Don't Twinkle, & 'Wrong way' Planets?
articles.summary: This article explains why stars appear to twinkle from Earth due to atmospheric distortion, while planets generally do not, offering a way to distinguish them. It discusses the origin of the word 'planet' as 'wanderer' and the concept of constellations. The piece also delves into the historical problem of 'wrong-way' or retrograde motion of planets, which challenged the ancient geocentric model and prefigured Galileo's revolutionary observations.

articles.title: Music in the Valley Event
articles.summary: The article details District Nine's "Music in the Valley" community event held on April 30, 2023, at Camden Community Center, which focused on showcasing local middle and high school music programs and community services. The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) participated with a booth, offering solar views and a UV solar bead activity. While attendance was lighter than previous years, SJAA successfully engaged with interested community members and connected with District 9 and PRNS staff.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: This article presents the "SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery" from the June 2023 edition of the SJAA EPHEMERIS. It features a collection of astrophotography images contributed by members such as PJ Mahany, Karen Bieber, Nikola Nikolov, and Hy Murveit. Each entry provides details on the celestial object captured, along with the date, location, and specific imaging equipment and software utilized by the astrophotographer.

articles.title: NASA's Perseverance Rover Captures View of Mars' Belva Crater
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover utilized its Mastcam-Z instrument to capture 152 images of Belva Crater, a 0.6-mile-wide impact crater within Mars' Jezero Crater. The resulting mosaic provides scientists with a 'natural roadcut' view into Jezero's geology, revealing exposed bedrock and steeply angled sedimentary layers. These features offer key insights into the crater's past, potentially indicating the presence of a large Martian sandbar formed by a river flowing into an ancient lake.

articles.title: NASA Pursues Lunar Terrain Vehicle Services for Artemis Missions
articles.summary: NASA is seeking industry proposals for a next-generation Lunar Terrain Vehicle (LTV) to enhance scientific exploration during Artemis missions, particularly in the Moon's south polar region. This LTV, intended for use starting with Artemis V in 2029, will be contracted as a service from industry and operate both with astronauts and as an uncrewed mobile science platform. This approach leverages commercial innovation to extend astronaut reach and scientific capabilities on the lunar surface.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: The 'Kid Spot' section features astronomy-themed jokes for children and introduces a 'Children's Activity Box' provided by the San Jose Astronomical Society (SJAA). This resource, containing art supplies and astronomy-themed coloring sheets, aims to keep young children occupied while adults attend to other tasks, such as working on equipment.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: This article from the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Board of Directors provides member announcements regarding online groups and open positions. It also details key discussions and decisions from the April, May, and June 2023 board meetings, covering financial approvals for equipment and services, progress on the Minors Policy and Code of Conduct, and operational updates like the 24" Dob task force and a new Zoom license for SIG meetings. The board also recognized Nancy Lieu with an Excellence Award.

articles.title: SJAA Library and Programs
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a wide array of resources and programs for members and the community, catering to all levels of astronomy enthusiasts. These include a library, free telescope repair, solar and night sky observing sessions, and beginner-friendly programs like Quick STARt. Additionally, SJAA provides an equipment loaner program, specialized astrophotography groups and workshops, and educational outreach through school star parties.
